title: tuning/minigames.json
description: The timing-bar minigame's presentation numbers. What is fixed here is that the file carries exactly one block, that block carries exactly four numbers, and each of them is bounded so a value that would make the game unplayable is refused rather than shipped. It governs a client-only presentation document rather than one of the sixteen balance files 21 §3.1 catalogues, which is why it carries no _status member: the three _status values each say how faithfully a document reproduces the design section that owns it, and no section owns this one. ⚠️ The name is one letter from schema/minigame.schema.json, which governs the Minigame SCREEN's loc keys — a different document with a different shape. The pairing table in ContentLayout declares content/minigame/ explicitly so the two cannot resolve into each other.

timingBar.description: Strike the Anvil (03 §6.2). 🔒 strikes is an integer because a strike is a press: the count is one more than the number of outcome tiers MG_TIMING_BAR authors in tuning/currencies.json, and nothing here can enforce that agreement across two documents — MinigameTuningDataTests does, and TimingBarRules refuses at runtime. The three fractions are bounded, not merely typed: a sweep of no duration leaves the cursor motionless, a half-width at or past 0.5 covers the whole bar and makes every press score, and a reduced-motion step of zero leaves a player who cannot watch a moving cursor with no way to aim at all. That the step must also be NARROWER than the window is a relation between two members rather than a bound on either, so it is pinned by the suite instead.

strikes.description: How many presses one game gives. At least one, because a game of no strikes cannot be played and would author a single-row reward table.

sweepSeconds.description: Seconds for one out-and-back sweep of the bar.

hitWindowHalfWidth.description: Half the scoring window's width, as a fraction of the bar, measured from its centre.

reducedMotionStepFraction.description: How far one press of the step control moves the cursor when the sweep is off, as a fraction of the bar.
